objects_changed.change: Added function.run require_manager as the first statement, input user_id = $auth.id.

templates_considered: AUTH-002: fits. Admin endpoints check the caller's role; used for the role check on the two protected endpoints.
AUTH-030: fits. Users can't make themselves admin; covers the role field in me PATCH.
AUTH-010: considered for login; already true for every endpoint in scope, not needed.
AUTH-040: middleware-based; no middleware exists and the ask is per-endpoint, so not used.
RET-001 / audit recipe: not in the ask; not used.

rules.covers: Refund approval only by managers (first statement role check)
Price changes only by managers (first statement role check)
Nobody can set role from request input, so no one can make themselves manager via me PATCH

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Staff can view but not change, across the whole app
Only managers may approve refunds: that the role check itself is correct
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check reads what a function decides; object.statement_required only confirms the call is first

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Nobody can get manager by any other route (admin endpoints, direct DB edits, data copies)
Who is allowed to be given the manager role

ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell: the ask says managers; I let admin pass too. Left as an assumption to confirm.

assumptions: Admin counts as manager for approvals and price changes.
Only the refund approval endpoint and the price endpoint are the 'approve refunds' and 'change prices' actions.
Dropping role from me PATCH and picking the three remaining fields is acceptable; the customer did not name it but it is required to close the self-promotion route.
function.run syntax with input = {...} and as $name is the right shape for this workspace.
confusions: The skill's policy file example shows params on one line with commas; I wrote a multi-line params block without commas and parse accepted it. Unclear whether that is the canonical style.

The paths param for object.statement_required uses {refund_id} as a path segment; the description says a {param} segment of the endpoint matches any segment, but it was not clear whether the literal braces must match the endpoint's own declared path. Parse did not warn, so I used the path as written in the endpoint.

Two rules in one policy under the AUTH-002 template key: the skill says extra rules go in a policy with a key of your own, but also says one policy per template. Chose AUTH-002 with two rules; unclear which the product wants.
function.run call shape: no example in the skill or catalogue of calling a custom function in an endpoint; I guessed function.run <name> { input = {...} } as $var.

$input|pick:[...] as a whole-body filter: the check text mentions pick as the last filter for mass assignment, but the endpoint change itself was a guess at the right data-filter syntax and at how db.patch treats omitted keys at runtime.
Whether a precondition with || in its expression is accepted: not verified by the dry run beyond push validation.
wished_for: A recipe or example for role-gated endpoints: a function.run role check as first statement, and the matching object.statement_required rule scoped by path.
A template for 'only role X may call these endpoints' that covers both the check and the self-promotion route (AUTH-002 plus AUTH-030 together) in one place.
Documentation of how db.patch treats omitted keys versus null, so a pick-based partial update is known to be safe.
A scope param for objects that read or write a named table with a given statement, e.g. all endpoints that db.patch products, to avoid hardcoding paths.
parse_errors_seen: AUTH-002.R1: Function "require_manager" is not on this branch (expected, function is new in this change)
AUTH-002.R2: Function "require_manager" is not on this branch (expected, function is new in this change)
why_confidence: The enforcement is a real function check on the two named endpoints and the self-promotion route is closed, so the stated rules match the ask. Confidence is not high because: the role check's logic is not verified by any check; function.run and pick syntax were not checked against a live parse of the workspace beyond the dry run; policy evaluate was not run; and staff-cannot-change is only covered for refunds and prices, not the whole app.
